_why_one_claim: R only, so there is no agreement claim; check.py records it as untested. RECOVERY asks whether the estimate is close to the parameter the fixture used, and harness/survival2_examples.test.py adds a second R implementation as an oracle.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process, Fine and Gray's (1999) own simulation design: F1(t | x) = 1 - [1 - 0.4 (1 - exp(-t))]^exp(-0.5 x)

agreement._note: In place of a second language, harness/survival2_examples.test.py fits survival::finegray with a weighted coxph clustered on the person: it agrees with crr to 1.1e-5 on the estimate and within 1e-3 on the standard error (0.12627 against 0.12623).

recovery.claim: the log subdistribution hazard ratio is close to the fixture's

calibration.limits: Measured in R by harness/survival2_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99. The committed fixture misses by 0.125.
